candidates.lead: The family of a woman who was murdered, along with her four children, say police failed to intervene
candidates.evidence_text: Failings contributed to Walkden arson attack deaths, family tells inquest - BBC News Image source, Family photos Image caption, Michelle Pearson (bottom right) and her four children, Demi,14, Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, were murdered in an arson attack at their home in Walkden Published 18 November 2026 The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard. Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children. The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders. Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths. The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son. Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017. 'Missed opportunities' Anna Morris KC, representing the Pearson family, said the ultimate culpability for the "heinous murders" was with the three perpetrators. But she said there had been "missed opportunities" and "cumulative failures" from authorities to stop and assess the risk the family were under from Bolland. "This was not an arson attack out of the blue by an unknown perpetrator," Morris added. The family believe a strategy meeting by Salford Council social workers should have been held to deal with the risk when Michelle presented as homeless through risk of violence. They say she should have been rehoused. They also say police failed to investigate and intervene after Bolland smashed her windows and set fire to her wheelie bin in the days before the fatal attack. He had walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute "no comment" interview when Greater Manchester Police decided to take no further action, the inquest heard. At the time, Bolland was on a "last chance" from a judge and serving a suspended jail sentence – and should have been arrested for breaking his bail conditions. Image source, PA Media Image caption, The family's home in Walkden was targeted with petrol bombs on 11 December 2017 The court heard that in the hours before the fatal attack, Bolland had again turned up on Michelle's doorstep and threatened to "do the house". The inquest heard police were called but believed that Bolland, who lived 350 yards away, was making "empty threats" and so did not arrest him. Officers instead went back to the station to complete paperwork and two hours later Bolland returned and firebombed the house. Morris said these failings probably contributed to the deaths in the arson attack. Fiona Barton KC, representing GMP, said the force had recognised their failings, but the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths. Barton said the coroner should not "speculate" as to what might have happened if police had tried to arrest Bolland after Michelle called police on the night of the attack. GMP admitted no attempt had been made to arrest Bolland, at the "most significant opportunity" to safeguard the family, which may have deterred him. But Barton said Bolland, who had taken drink and drugs, was not deterred by seeing a police car outside the house. She said he had returned with petrol bombs once the car had left. 'Pure speculation' Barton told the hearing that response officers making decisions to close investigations now faced strategic oversight and more support and direction. "In 2017, which was when sadly this tragic event took place, GMP was a failing force under special measures," she added. "It is in a very different place today." Sam Green, representing seven GMP officers who had dealt with incidents at the house, said any failings of officers could not be said to have probably contributed to the fatal arson attack. Green said Bolland had been told by a judge he was "drinking in the last chance saloon" but continued to commit crime, adding that to suggest police action would have prevented him carrying out the attack was "pure speculation". candidates.summary: Shabir Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after 14 years behind bars
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.

candidates.lead: Shabir Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after 14 years behind bars
candidates.evidence_text: Government 'determined' to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader - BBC News Image source, GMP Image caption, Shabir Ahmed was the head of a gang in Rochdale which abused girls as young as 12 Published 18 November 2026 The government is still considering "every option" to deport Rochdale grooming gang leader Shabir Ahmed, a Home Office minister has said, months after ministers suggested emergency legislation could be used to remove him from the UK. Ahmed, 73, was released from prison in July after serving 14 years for rape and other sexual offences against girls, some as young as 12. The government said at the time that it would seek to deport Ahmed to Pakistan. Having been stripped of his British citizenship, he now holds only Pakistani nationality. However, he remains in the UK because existing legislation prevents the deportation of some Commonwealth citizens. A minister said earlier that officials were "determined" to remove him from the country. Image source, ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock Image caption, Vulnerable girls in Rochdale were plied with drinks and drugs by the grooming gang Lord Collins of Highbury was asked in the House of Lords whether the Home Office had threatened Pakistan with the withdrawal of foreign aid or visa sanctions. Lord Collins replied: "We are pursuing every option to deport Shabir Ahmed. We talk to a range of countries about returns and deportations, but it would be inappropriate for us to give a running commentary on discussions." He added that the Immigration and Asylum Bill gave ministers extra powers to deport "the vilest foreign criminals". 'Very rare act' Lord Collins continued that the government had deported nearly 12,000 foreign criminals in the two years since it came to office. He added: "We have deprived Ahmed of his citizenship, the United Kingdom citizenship, a very rare act to take. We are determined to ensure that he is deported." The government has been examining ways to deport Ahmed since his release. The 1971 law forbids the removal of a small group of Commonwealth citizens who arrived in the UK more than 50 years ago. Reports have suggested Pakistan might not accept Ahmed because he had renounced his citizenship, but a Number 10 spokesperson previously confirmed that officials had raised the issue with counterparts in Islamabad. Shadow Home Office minister Lord Cameron of Lochiel said: "Removing the legal barrier to his deportation is pointless if the Pakistani government refuses to accept him." candidates.lead: The boy died in hospital three days after an incident at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton, police say
candidates.evidence_text: Police investigate death of boy, 3, after nursery incident - BBC News Image caption, The boy died in hospital three days after the incident at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton, police said By Angela Ferguson North West Published 18 November 2026 An investigation has been launched into the death of a three-year-old boy following an incident at a nursery in Greater Manchester, police said. The boy became critically ill at Cosy Toes Nursery in Middleton shortly before 16:00 GMT on Monday 2 November. He was rushed to hospital, where he died three days later. Greater Manchester Police said his family were being supported by specialist officers. Det Ch Insp Claire Brennan said: "This is an incredibly tragic development in a deeply upsetting incident and our thoughts remain with the boy's family." Police said an investigation had been launched in line with standard procedure following a child's death in a care setting. No arrests have been made at this time. 'Wonderful boy' A spokeswoman for Cosy Toes said they were "all heartbroken" by the "wonderful and beautiful" boy's death. "Our thoughts and prayers are all with his family at this terrible time," she said. "We will of course give our fullest possible assistance in every way possible to the enquiries that must rightly follow this tragic event." Anyone with information about the boy's death is being urged to contact police. Brennan said: "We are in the very early stages of our involvement and are carefully considering events and the evidence available to us. "For now, we ask that the family's privacy is respected as they begin to navigate the unimaginable loss of their little boy." Ofsted said it had taken the decision to suspend the nursery's registration in the wake of the incident, meaning the nursery will be closed for six weeks as investigations are carried out. A spokesperson said: "Our thoughts are with the family of the young boy and everyone affected by this deeply distressing and tragic incident. "We have worked closely with the police, and we have suspended the nursery's registration. We will continue to support the police and other agencies in their enquiries. We are unable to comment further while the police investigation is ongoing." candidates.lead: Seven people are now in custody over the death of a 27-year-old man in north Manchester
candidates.evidence_text: Six more arrests in Crumpsall murder investigation over stab death - BBC News Image caption, A 27-year-old man was stabbed to death in Crumpsall on Saturday By Marc Waddington North West Published 18 November 2026 Six more people have been arrested as part of a murder probe launched after a man was stabbed to death. A 27-year-old man died in Moss Bank in Crumpsall, Manchester, shortly after 01:30 GMT on Saturday, following an attack by "a number of males". Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said it had arrested two men on suspicion of murder, and four other people on suspicion of assisting an offender. Another man arrested after the incident on suspicion of murder, remains in custody, the force said. The victim was reported to have been set upon by a number of men wearing balaclavas. Of the seven people held as part of the investigation, two are men, aged 24 and 25, who are being questioned on suspicion of murder. Two men, aged 33 and 35, and two women, aged 21 and 34, are being questioned on suspicion of assisting an offender. The other murder suspect is a 26-year-old man, the force said. Det Insp Neil Higginson said: "Our investigation is continuing at a pace and we now have six more people in our custody. "Even though we have made seven arrests in total, we are continuing to investigate this tragic death and are appealing for the public to assist us. "I would still urge anyone who witnessed the incident, saw the movements of vehicles, or has any information that could assist our investigation to contact us however insignificant you think it might be." candidates.evidence_text: Ex-football chief who plotted to rape man's wife admits child abuse image offences - BBC News Image caption, Karl Lindsay stood down as chief executive of Taunton Town Football Club last year Published 18 November 2026 A former chief executive of a non-league football club who plotted to drug and rape a man's wife has pleaded guilty to separate child abuse image offences. Karl Lindsay, who stepped down from his post at Taunton Town in Somerset last year, last month admitted charges of conspiracy to rape and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent to stupefy. The 56-year-old had pleaded guilty shortly before he was due to go on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court alongside nine other men who deny their alleged roles in the abuse of the wife in Stockport. He appeared at the same court earlier by prison videolink and entered more guilty pleas to offences not connected with the ongoing trial. Lindsay, of Taunton, admitted three offences of making indecent images of children between February 2024 and November 2025. He made 10 still images and eight moving images classed as category A, the most serious, two moving class B images, and 11 still class C images. Lindsay also admitted two counts of possessing extreme pornography involving a person performing a sexual act on an animal and another relating to an act which threatened a person's life. Judge Maurice Greene further remanded Lindsay into custody and said he would be sentenced after the conclusion of the ongoing trial. The husband at the centre of the Manchester trial, who cannot be named to protect his wife's anonymity, pleaded guilty in September to a series of offences dating from 2004 including rape, sexual assault and administering a substance with intent to commit a sexual offence. The man, in his 60s and from Stockport, will give evidence later this month against the nine defendants who deny various allegations, including rape and conspiracy to rape, between 2015 and 2025. He will also be sentenced at a later date. candidates.evidence_text: Police now using scrapped Clean Air Zone cameras to catch criminals - BBC News Image source, Getty Images Image caption, More than 1,300 signs were installed for Greater Manchester's abandoned charging scheme By Haider Saleem , North West and Declan Carey , Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 18 November 2026 Police have been catching criminals by using cameras installed as part of an abandoned Clean Air Zone scheme. Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone. And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said. The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly. Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference. "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said. Deputy Mayor Kate Green said: "They are not speed cameras, they are being used for crime detection and as an investigative tool." The cameras automatically read passing vehicles' registration plates and check them against records of vehicles of interest. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The cameras were installed to enforce a charging scheme that was later abandoned Before the handover on 13 July, police had to request access to images and information held by Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM), rather than receive the data directly. In September 2025, GMP said information from ANPR cameras had helped investigations into 63 major and serious crimes over a 28-month period, including murder, robbery and firearms offences. A report to the panel on 16 November confirmed the cameras had been integrated into GMP's existing network and were operational. Privacy concerns A six-week public consultation received 4,830 responses, with almost 90% supporting the change to police use. However, about 38% of respondents identified protection of their privacy as a concern, while 37% raised questions about how their data might be shared. GMP said its system recorded registration numbers from all passing vehicles, including those not suspected of crime. The information is retained on the national system for one year, with access restricted under policing rules. Camera information will also be shared with TfGM for transport planning and monitoring the replacement clean air plan, but the transport body will not have access to a live feed. evidence_texts: Police have been catching criminals by using cameras installed as part of an abandoned Clean Air Zone scheme Greater Manchester Police (GMP) took control of about 400 automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that were supposed to be used to enforce the planned region-wide low-emission zone And they have been used to make "multiple arrests", a senior officer said The cameras were installed as part of Greater Manchester's drive to cut the number of high-emission vehicles on the regions roads, but the plans were dropped in favour of other efforts to make the region's transport network more environmentally friendly Deputy chief constable Terry Woods told Greater Manchester's police, fire and crime panel on Monday the system was making a significant difference "It's been tangible, multiple arrests on the back of that system and it's keeping people safe," he said

candidates.evidence_text: The family of a mother who was murdered in an arson attack along with her four youngest children have said failings by police and local authorities contributed to their deaths, an inquest heard Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017

On May 25 this year, Aspinall was found in an address at the Freehold estate in Rochdale . Mr Howard, Tweedale Street, Rochdale, had previously pleaded not guilty to the single charge However, he entered a guilty plea on the first day of his trial at Manchester Crown Court on Monday (November 16). He was sentenced to life behind bars with a minimum term of 21 years by Judge Nicholas Dean KC at Manchester Crown Court today (November 18) On Sunday May 25, 2026, police were called to reports of a concern for welfare at the property off Tweedale Street. Howard, 37, had made the call himself, telling the call handler he had stabbed Ms Aspinall to death two days earlier, and was reporting the crime because her body w Ms Aspinall, known to friends as ‘Kiki’, was pronounced dead at the scene by police officers and paramedics. She was found with strangle wounds, a slash to her neck and stab wound on the right side of her chest

english_fact_card.what_happened: A beauty influencer known as the 'Lip King' was shown laughing and complaining 'I'm exhausted' while carrying out a fatal Brazilian butt lift on a mother-of-five, Alice Webb, 33. She became unwell during the procedure on September 23, 2024, and died in hospital. The practitioner, Jordan Parke, gave her seven times the recommended amount of filler before she collapsed and went into cardiac arrest. Parke was under investigation for gross negligence manslaughter but died earlier this year from a suspected cosmetic procedure while on bail.

Greater Manchester Police said officers attended the address at 2.22pm to make an arrest attempt as part of an ongoing and unrelated investigation A force spokesperson said: "Emergency services attended the scene, and officers recovered ammunition and discovered potentially hazardous substances. Add to preferred sources Comments News Less than half a year ago, Jacob Hicken felt a ‘deep despair’ about his future. “I didn’t get on with school,” the 16-year-old said. “Not too long ago I was going down, you could say, a bad path “It felt like the teachers were out for me. Not being in the right crowds, not being around the right people, not having someone telling you this ain’t it “Sometimes it feels like there’s not much out there for young people in Salford . When you come from a council estate, you feel like there’s no help for you. You’re a product of your environment.” He is one of a growing number of youngsters in the borough who was classified as in danger of becoming a ‘NEET’ – those between 16 and 24 not in education, employment, or training. It’s a hot topic nationally, with the publication of the Milburn Review on Tuesday, November 19 The 278-page report sets out a host of far-reaching policy suggestions to start combatting what Alan Milburn has described as the ‘moral crisis’ of the UK’s 981,000 out-of-work young people

With that responsibility comes great scrutiny However, for some, temptation proved too much. In March 2026, the Ministry of Justice stated that between 2020 and 2025, 41 prison officers had been convicted of an offence of misconduct in a public office , where the offence related to an inappropriate relationship with a prison The Prison Service has since developed a scheme, the Enable programme, which designed to assist trainees with professional practice, capability and strengthening learning It is currently piloting a regional delivery model across London prisons and testing the model in Early Adopter sites, the service said. A redesigned Foundation Training programme for new prison officers is also being developed, with testing due to begin in 2027 A Prison Service spokesperson said: “Prison officers are the backbone of our service, working every day in some of the toughest conditions. That is why getting training right is essential to delivering punishment that works to cut crime."

candidates.evidence_text: Newton Heath Manchester tower block evacuated with 70 flats suddenly closed off amid 'urgent' concerns The tenants of more than 70 flats in Newton Heath have been moved out Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter a A north Manchester tower block has been evacuated due to 'urgent' safety concerns. Tenants in more than 70 council flats in Shackleton Court, Newton Heath , have been told they have to leave their homes by today (Wednesday) It comes after builders found a problem with a concrete panel while carrying out refurbishment work on the 15 storey block. Manchester council said residents are now being found alternative accommodation while repairs are carried out Businessman Dishad Ali, 41, who lives in a 13th floor flat with his wife and two-year-old daughter, said: "We were told yesterday we had to be out by today. A camera caught the car When police letters about the offence went unanswered, the Dutch defender, who is one of the Premier League's fastest players, was also accused of failing to confirm who was driving the car at the time. candidates.evidence_text: Courts The secrets that led to the downfall of five prison officers The Prison Service in England and Wales have developed a scheme given to trainees to help them avoid being manipulated into illicit relationships by experienced criminals Top row, lef Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 06:01, 19 Nov 2026 Updated 07:42, 19 Nov 2026 It's a position held in the highest regard with the intense responsibility of guarding the most violent in our society. With that responsibility comes great scrutiny However, for some, temptation proved too much. In March 2026, the Ministry of Justice stated that between 2020 and 2025, 41 prison officers had been convicted of an offence of misconduct in a public office , where the offence related to an inappropriate relationship with a prison The Prison Service has since developed a scheme, the Enable programme, which designed to assist trainees with professional practice, capability and strengthening learning It is currently piloting a regional delivery model across London prisons and testing the model in Early Adopter sites, the service said. A redesigned Foundation Training programme for new prison officers is also being developed, with testing due to begin in 2027 A Prison Service spokesperson said: “Prison officers are the backbone of our service, working every day in some of the toughest conditions. That is why getting training right is essential to delivering punishment that works to cut crime."

A police investigation is now underway Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news report A three-year-old boy has tragically died after emergency crews were called to a nursery in Middleton Emergency services were called to the Cosy Toes nursery on Mainway East to reports of concern for a child on November 2. On May 25 this year, Aspinall was found in an address at the Freehold estate in Rochdale . Mr Howard, Tweedale Street, Rochdale, had previously pleaded not guilty to the single charge However, he entered a guilty plea on the first day of his trial at Manchester Crown Court on Monday (November 16). He was sentenced to life behind bars with a minimum term of 21 years by Judge Nicholas Dean KC at Manchester Crown Court today (November 18) On Sunday May 25, 2026, police were called to reports of a concern for welfare at the property off Tweedale Street. Howard, 37, had made the call himself, telling the call handler he had stabbed Ms Aspinall to death two days earlier, and was reporting the crime because her body w Ms Aspinall, known to friends as ‘Kiki’, was pronounced dead at the scene by police officers and paramedics. She was found with strangle wounds, a slash to her neck and stab wound on the right side of her chest

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Real Life Manchester boy suffers devastating injuries in Benidorm after falling 60ft from balcony Jamie suffered devastating injuries in the fall from the sixth-floor balcony Add to preferred sources News Faye Mayern and Ashlie Blakey Live and breakin A 17-year-old boy has suffered devastating injuries after falling 60ft from the balcony of a hotel in Benidorm Jamie, from Manchester, was staying at the SOL Pelícanos Ocas hotel, the hotel used for filming the hit TV show Benidorm, with his mum, Gemma, and her friends when the incident happed on November 10. The teenager, whose family do not want his surname shared, was rushed to hospita Doctors found he had suffered extensive fractures to both sides of chest and a punctured lung. He also ruptured an artery in the fall, as well as breaking his pelvis, both legs and one arm, and had to undergo life-saving surgery Doctors have warned his family he could be facing paralysis. His loved ones have now launched a GoFundMe for help to bring him back to the UK His aunt Lauren Baker said: "Jamie is a charmer and a loveable rogue. The doctors have serious concerns about his recovery particularly with paralysis but we don't know what the outcome will be

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

The organisers of today’s day of rugby league at the stadium in Salford have already had to cancel the pyrotechnics; the wind speeds are too high I’m here to watch a gilded amateur rugby league tradition brought back to life, and I’ll soon be joined by more than a thousand people. candidates.evidence_text: Michelle Pearson, 37, died nearly two years after her home in Walkden, Salford, was firebombed on 11 December 2017, killing her four youngest children The inquest at Bolton Coroner's Court heard Michelle had called police several times and told social workers she wanted to move before the murders Final submissions from lawyers for the family, Greater Manchester Police and others were heard earlier. GMP said the evidence did not support that their inaction had probably caused or contributed to the deaths The murders came after a feud involving mother-of-six Michelle's eldest son Zak Bolland, 26, his accomplice David Worrall, 28, and Bolland's girlfriend, Courtney Brierley, 20, were all jailed over the fatal attack in December 2017 Anna Morris KC, representing the Pearson family, said the ultimate culpability for the "heinous murders" was with the three perpetrators

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester will come together under one sky this weekend as free fireworks celebrations return to light up the night sky on Saturday 7 November at three Manchester parks: Heaton Park, Wythenshawe Park and Platt Fields Park This year's events have been designed with sustainability, affordability and accessibility at their heart, ensuring the celebrations can be enjoyed by as many people as possible Affordability is a key focus, with a range of free activities and entertainment on offer throughout the evening and people are encouraged to take part in the Lantern Parade at 7pm prior to the main firework display. Visitors can also enjoy value-for-money funfair rides, with 95% The events have been planned to cater for a wide audience, including those who would prefer to attend an earlier, shorter, lower-noise display. Hosting three large-scale events across the city also helps reduce the environmental impact associated with multiple smaller community d A number of measures have been introduced to improve sustainability. Avoidable single-use plastics have been removed from all event sites, the pyrotechnics supplier uses sustainable packaging, and post-event litter picks will take place immediately after the celebrations. Local s In a bid to reduce food waste, any surplus food will, where possible, be redistributed through local charities and community projects in partnership with the Our Manchester Food Partnership

candidates.evidence_text: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council Manchester’s air quality has improved significantly in recent years due to investment in public transport and cycling and walking routes, cleaner vehicle technology including electric vehicles and stricter national emissions standards. The investment-led Greater Manchester Clean But while good progress has been made, the Council wants to go further because environmental air pollution remains a real health risk, especially for people in more disadvantaged communities or with existing health conditions who can be more vulnerable to its effects The Vision is simple: “Manchester will be a city where everyone can breathe cleaner air and live healthier lives.” Alongside it sits a headline action plan which will guide further measures to improve air quality across the city, based around four priorities Reduce people’s exposure to air pollution, prioritising the most vulnerable such as children and people with existing health conditions and communities where the potential health benefits are the greatest

candidates.lead: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12 The cost of living is a major concern for many, and it may get tougher during the winter, as such, the event and the targeted support offered to people across Bolton offer some reassurance to those worst affected The support spans a large number of areas including helping access emergency food, heating, and financial assistance The event brings those organisations providing support together so they can better understand what is available across the town and as such can make informed decisions about who to refer people to for the most appropriate help In total there were over 40 organisations attending the event including the public, voluntary, and community sector, and other parters who were highlighting their services all were encouraged to network, share information, and create a more connected and efficient framework The presentations highlighted how Bolton’s Tacking Poverty Strategy can make a real difference, and how the Crisis, and Resilience Fund is being allocated to help groups across the borough

evidence_packet.lead: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12 The cost of living is a major concern for many, and it may get tougher during the winter, as such, the event and the targeted support offered to people across Bolton offer some reassurance to those worst affected The support spans a large number of areas including helping access emergency food, heating, and financial assistance The event brings those organisations providing support together so they can better understand what is available across the town and as such can make informed decisions about who to refer people to for the most appropriate help In total there were over 40 organisations attending the event including the public, voluntary, and community sector, and other parters who were highlighting their services all were encouraged to network, share information, and create a more connected and efficient framework The presentations highlighted how Bolton’s Tacking Poverty Strategy can make a real difference, and how the Crisis, and Resilience Fund is being allocated to help groups across the borough

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . evidence_packet.summary: Five days. Five themes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

candidates.evidence_text: BBC Casualty star Anna Chell will take to the stage at Manchester theatre 53two this Christmas as part of the cast of A Trifle And A Turkey Crown , alongside actor and 53two Creative Director Simon Naylor The premiere, written by Rebekah Harrison, who is no stranger to The Arches, runs from Wed 16 Dec – Wed 23 Dec. It tells the story of four people, living in a Northern town, whose lives begin to intertwine as Christmas approaches “ A Trifle And A Turkey Crown offers audiences something different: a contemporary Christmas story centred on ordinary lives, unexpected relationships and the connections that can form between people who have been living only metres apart.” For Chell, the production also represents something of a return home. Before establishing herself on screen, Anna trained with Manchester Actors Platform, the actor-training and development organisation that would later evolve into 53two She went on to build a successful career across stage and screen and is now best known to television audiences as Jodie Whyte in BBC’s long-running medical drama Casualty , a role she first took on in 2023 and in which she has since become a series regular Now, many years after training with Manchester Actors Platform, she returns to the organisation’s home as part of 53two’s Christmas production

From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: The Bridgewater Hall , City Centre 19 November 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit In 1996, Thomas Adès wrote a work celebrating the opening of The Bridgewater Hall – a four-minute showpiece, These Premises Are Alarmed , that the Observer called “packed with detailed, fascinating invention.” But for all its “utmost, fine-grained, virtuosity,” it doesn’t take it Adès also conducts his own Asyla , the piece that made his name in the years just after. The title is the Latin plural of “asylum”, which can mean both a place of refuge and an institution for the insane – and the piece plays on this plurality. Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. Hailed by the LA Times as “an outright sensation”, Smith writes music drawn from field recordings and underwater microphones, looking for what she c The evening closes with Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite , one of the happiest accidents in musical history. Sergei Diaghilev, head of the Ballets Russes, saw his first three choices to score a new ballet fall through before he gambled on an unproven 27-year-old; Stravinsky himself la Four works, then, that each began as a risk on someone (to varying degrees) untested – Stravinsky in 1910, Adès in 1996, Smith tonight. If this is Adès’s opening statement as Principal Guest Conductor, it’s a heartening one: a little faith in emerging composers can go a long way

candidates.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC JJ Gabriel sparks concern in Spain with ex-Man United star on verge of joining new club JJ Gabriel looks set to join Real Madrid after controversially announcing his departure from Manchester United. The 16-year-old, who’s expected to join Real Madrid, confirmed his decision to leave in a video on social media earlier this week, where he thanked staff and teammates for their suppor The Manchester Evening News understands that higher-ups at Old Trafford were disappointed to be caught off guard by the Instagram post . Add to preferred sources Reform UK in Manchester is demanding ‘full transparency’ after claiming Manchester City funded an event for councillors in May with an unlimited free bar, ‘executive’ catering, and live music The Reform UK group has submitted a public motion about the matter which will be debated by councillors in a meeting next Wednesday (November 25) According to the Reform motion, the event was held at Depot Mayfield on May 25 with Manchester’s Lord Mayor Shaukat Ali inviting councillors to a civic reception to celebrate the football club’s achievements at the end of the season That year saw Manchester City FC men's team win the FA Cup and League Cup double, the women's team win the League and FA Cup double and the youth team win the FA Youth Cup. It also marked the final season of Pep Guardiola's time as manager of the men's team But Manchester Reform claim it was not made clear that the football club had funded the event

A Champions League winner, a Premier League winner and an FA Cup winner after an incredible season with Manchester City Now the England international is at a significant crossroads. He's missed the last four matches with loan club Everton owing to a disciplinary breach and while he could return to action this weekend against Brentford his long-term future is uncertain The arrival of Enzo Maresca at the Etihad in the summer, someone with whom Grealish forged a close bond during the 2022-23 season when the Italian was on Pep Guardiola's coaching staff, was viewed by some as a potential olive branch for the 31-year-old Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! The £300m year-round entertainment, dining and cultural destination at Etihad Campus opened earlier this year with a new string of restaurants, The latest is Brickworks Market Hall, which is bringing together some of Manchester’s best-known independent operators under one roof. It features a wide mix of food offerings and two brand new bars Situated on the main square, fronting onto both the Etihad Stadium and Co-op Live, Brickworks Market Hall is currently open pre-and-post Etihad Stadium match days and Co-op Live events. Its food line up spans pizzas, Japanese street food, burgers, fried chicken and pies, as well Spanning 357sqm with capacity for 238 covers, Brickworks has been designed as a 'vibrant, bustling space' where flavours and concepts collide.
